newsitem.title: USA: Midwest economic expansion seen continuing--report.
newsitem.headline: Midwest economic expansion seen continuing--report.

text.p: The Midwest's economic expansion of recent years, the second longest since World War Two, is expected to continue, First Chicago NBD Corp's deputy chief economist reported in the July First Forecasts newsletter.
Preliminary data shows growth slowed in the second quarter of this year, but prospects for the third quarter are slightly better, Diane Swonk wrote.
The First Chicago NBD Great Lakes Index is expected to show a 1.7 percent increase in the second quarter, slightly behind the real growth in Gross Domestic Product, Swonk wrote.
Third quarter estimates predict a 2.3 percent increase, slightly ahead of real growth in Gross Domestic Product, however, Swonk found.
First Chicago measures the output of goods and services from Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio and Wisconsin to create the index.
Key changes to Midwest business such as widespread restructuring and production streamlining have made the region a "case study" for the rest of the country, Swonk wrote.
The expansion has led to a drop in welfare rolls, increased real estate values and surges in state and local tax revenues with more benefits to come, Swonk wrote.

"Real wages (net of benefits) are showing signs of accelerating and recent productivity gains give us reason to believe that this economy will eventually deliver measurable real wage gains," Swonk wrote.
